facts.claim: Social association does not reflect stimulus familiarity per se, that it can modify perception, that it can both occur automatically and alter expectancies.
facts.quote: Evidence using this procedure suggests that social association does not reflect stimulus familiarity per se, that it can modify perception, that it can both occur automatically and alter expectancies

facts.claim: Judgements of inefficient actions were biased towards the efficient prediction.
facts.quote: Judgements of inefficient actions were biased towards the efficient prediction (straight trajectories upward to avoid the obstruction, arched trajectories downward towards the target).

facts.claim: Investors do exhibit familiarity bias when choosing between different companies to invest in.
facts.quote: The results of this exploratory study indicate that investors do exhibit familiarity bias when choosing between different companies to invest in.

facts.claim: Familiarity with novel foods and curiosity both led to higher acceptance.
facts.quote: Familiarity with novel foods and curiosity both led to higher acceptance.
facts.causalWarning: causal wording, but the cited study only shows an association

research.angle: While familiarity can increase acceptance of foods and influence investment choices, social associations are distinct from simple stimulus familiarity and can actively modify perception.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that familiarity and social associations influence perception and decision-making, but they are not always synonymous with simple repeated exposure.
research.caveat: The sources do not provide direct evidence on the 'mere exposure' effect specifically regarding the development of trust or intimacy in human relationships.
